Release on the other object. When you start or end the drag on an anchor, that anchor is used; otherwise the closest pair of anchors of the two objects is used. The connector is an open line with no fill and the default outline. Connector settings The property bar, shown with the connector tools and when the selection is all connectors, has the three kinds of connector (with connectors selected, they change how those run), the corner radius of rounded connectors (3 mm at first), and the outline width, style and arrowheads of the selected connectors. Staying attached When you move, scale or reshape the joined objects, the connector runs again between their anchors. When you move the connector together with its objects, it stays attached. When you move the connector on its own, it lets go and becomes a plain line. Undo attaches it again. When one of its objects is deleted, the connector stays where it is. Editing anchors The Edit Anchor tool adds, moves and deletes anchors: Choose the Edit Anchor tool and click an object. Its anchors show as diamonds. Click inside the object to add an anchor there. Drag an anchor you added to move it. Select an anchor and press Delete, double-click it, or click Delete anchor on the property bar to remove it. Remove all custom anchors removes every anchor you added. The four anchors at the middle of the sides cannot be removed.

Objekty, symboly a vrstvy Každý tvar, čára, text a obrázek v kresbě je objekt. Tyto stránky vysvětlují, jak objekty vybírat, přesouvat, měnit jejich velikost, otáčet je a zarovnávat, jak je řadit, seskupovat a uspořádat do vrstev a jak je znovu používat jako symboly. Věnují se i objektům s vlastním úkolem: tabulkám, čárovým a QR kódům, komentářům a datům připojeným k objektům.

h: The Pick tool Moving, resizing and turning Dragging with the right button The property bar Selection groups The Freehand Pick tool
x: Selecting objects Before you change an object, you select it. The Pick tool (Space switches to it from most tools, and Space again takes you back to the tool you were using) selects, moves and resizes objects; the Freehand Pick tool does the same but selects with a freehand loop. The Pick tool Click an object to select it. A filled object counts where it is filled; an unfilled one on its outline. Text, groups, tables and pictures count anywhere inside their box. Shift+click adds an object to the selection or takes it out. Drag around objects, starting on an empty spot: the objects wholly inside the dashed frame are selected. Hold Alt as you finish the drag to select every object the frame touches. Hold Shift to turn over the objects the frame takes: those selected are deselected and the others added. Hold Ctrl to keep the frame square. Ctrl+click selects an object inside a group, one level further in at each click. Its handles are round, and changes act on it alone; drag it from anywhere on it to move it alone. Ctrl+click on a clip frame starts editing its contents instead (see Clip frames). Alt+click selects the object beneath the selected one, to reach objects that are covered. Tab and Shift+Tab select the next or previous object. Esc selects nothing. Edit > Select All and a double-click on the tool's button select every object; Select All also selects all text, guidelines or nodes. The selected objects show eight square handles around them and a small cross in the middle. The status bar says what is selected and on which layer. The pointer shows the move arrows only over what is selected. Over any other object it keeps the plain arrow, since a press there picks that object first; dragging an unselected object still picks and moves it. A right click while you drag a selection frame is ignored: the frame goes on and selects when you let go of the left button. Drawing and shaping tools whose click has no job of its own (the rectangle, ellipse, polygon and other shape tools, the Knife, the connectors, Blend and others) select too: click an object to select it, Shift+click to add or take it away, Ctrl+click to reach into groups, and click empty space to select nothing. A drag still draws. The line tools and the Text tool keep their clicks. Moving, resizing and turning Drag a selected object, or the cross in its middle, to move it. Hold Ctrl to move only horizontally or vertically. The object snaps to what snapping is set to. Drag a corner handle to resize in proportion, a side handle to stretch in one direction. Hold Shift to resize from the center, Ctrl to resize in steps of 100% (crossing the other side mirrors the object), Alt to resize freely. Click a selected object again to show the rotation handles: drag a curved corner arrow to rotate, a side arrow to skew. Hold Ctrl for steps of 15 degrees. Drag the ring in the middle to turn about another point; double-click it to put it back in the middle. In this rotate mode, a node of the selection (or the middle of a segment) dragged turns the selection about the ring; let go near another object's edge and the node lands exactly on it, so an arc turned about one end can be laid onto a line. The rotate handle still snaps to other objects' nodes, midpoints and centres to aim the turn at one. While dragging, press Space or click the right button to leave a copy where the objects were; Esc cancels the drag. The arrow keys nudge the selection by the nudge distance (2.54 mm at first), with Shift by the super nudge distance and with Ctrl by the micro nudge distance. Set them on the Rulers page of the document options. + duplicates the selection in place. Dragging with the right button Drag a selected object with the right mouse button. When you release, a menu offers to move it there, copy it there, copy its fill, outline or all its properties to the object under the pointer, or place it inside that object as a clip frame. The property bar With nothing selected, the property bar shows the page size and orientation, the drawing units and the nudge distance. With a selection, it shows the position (X and Y), the size (W and H), the scale, the rotation angle, the mirror buttons, the outline width, to front and to back, and convert to curves. Text adds the text settings, and bitmaps the bitmap commands. With several objects, a group or a curve of several parts, it adds group, ungroup, combine, break apart, the shaping commands and the Align and Distribute panel. Selection groups Press Ctrl and a number from 0 to 9 to remember the selection under that number. Press the number alone to select those objects again, and again to zoom to them. Alt and the number add the selection to the group. Groups are saved with the drawing. The Freehand Pick tool The Freehand Pick tool works like the Pick tool, but a drag from an empty spot draws a loop. When you release, every object wholly inside the loop is selected; hold Alt as you release to select every object the loop touches, Shift to add to the selection. Hold Ctrl to draw a rectangle instead. The options of the Pick tool, such as whether a frame selects the objects it touches, are on the Pick page of the tool options; see Tool options.

h: The Transformations panel Position Rotate Scale and Mirror Size Skew The Free Transform tool Undoing transformations The Coordinates panel
x: Moving, scaling, rotating and skewing You can transform objects by dragging them with the Pick tool (see Selecting objects), by typing values on the property bar, with the Free Transform tool, or precisely with the Transformations panel. The Transformations panel Open the panel with Object > Transformations, or with Alt+F7 (Position), Alt+F8 (Rotate), Alt+F9 (Scale and Mirror) and Alt+F10 (Size). The buttons at the top choose one of five pages.  Every page ends with the reference point, a 3 by 3 grid that chooses the point of the selection that is placed, turned about or kept still (the center at first), Copies and Apply. Distances are in the drawing units, angles in degrees (counterclockwise), scales in percent. To transform the selection: Choose a page and type the values. Choose the reference point. Set Copies: 0 changes the selection itself; a number above 0 leaves the selection as it is and adds that many copies, each transformed once more than the one before. The copies are one undo step, and the last copy becomes the selection, so another Apply goes on from there. Click Apply. Position X and Y move the selection. With Relative position on (at first), they are a distance to move by; off, they are where the reference point goes, counted from the ruler origin. With Relative position on, the grid picks a direction: a side or a corner sets the distance to the selection's size, so each copy lands right next to the last one. Rotate Type the angle, and the Center to turn about. With Relative center on (at first), the center is counted from the reference point; off, from the ruler origin. Scale and Mirror X and Y scale in percent (100% at first). Mirror horizontally and Mirror vertically flip the selection. Proportional keeps both scales the same. Size W and H set the width and height of the selection. Proportional keeps the proportions. Skew X and Y slant the selection by angles. With Use anchor point on, the reference point stays still; off, the center does. The Free Transform tool The Free Transform tool, in the Pick flyout, transforms the selection about the point where you press. Choose a mode on the property bar: Free rotation (at first): turns the selection around the press point. Free angle reflection: mirrors the selection across the line from the press point to the pointer; moving the pointer turns that line. Free scale: scales about the press point. Free skew: horizontal movement skews horizontally, vertical movement vertically. Hold Alt to scale, Ctrl to skew or Shift to reflect for one drag, whatever the mode. With Apply to duplicate on, the press makes a copy and the drag transforms the copy, leaving the original as it was. The property bar also has the position, size, scale, angle and mirror fields. Undoing transformations Object > Clear Transformations takes the selected objects back to how they were before they were scaled, rotated or skewed. The Coordinates panel The Coordinates panel draws an object from typed coordinates, or reshapes the selected one, with a dashed preview on the drawing. Open it from Window > Panels.  Choose the kind of object with the buttons at the top: rectangle or square, ellipse or circle, polygon or regular polygon, star, complex star, 2-point line or multipoint curve. Type its values: rectangles and ellipses: the position of the origin point (chosen in a 3 by 3 grid), the width and height, the angle of rotation, and the corners of the bounding box while the angle is 0; squares and circles: the position, the side or diameter and the angle; polygons and stars: the number of points or sides, the sharpness, the angle and the circle the points lie on; regular polygons: the number of sides, the length of a side, the angle and the center; 2-point lines: the start point and end point, or the length and angle; multipoint curves: the list of points, with buttons to add and delete points and to close the curve. Instead of typing, click a button with a pointer and target, then click or drag on the drawing to set that value. A right click cancels. Click Create object to add it, or Replace object to reshape the selected rectangle, ellipse, polygon or curve while keeping its fill, outline, name and place. Positions are counted from the ruler origin, in the drawing units.

h: Aligning Distributing Fit objects to a path
x: Aligning and distributing objects Aligning lines objects up by their edges or centers; distributing spaces them evenly. Use the Align and Distribute panel (Ctrl+Shift+A), the commands of Object > Align and Distribute, or the keys below.  Aligning Select the objects. Select the one the others should line up with last. In the Align part of the panel, choose Align to: Active object (at first): the object selected last; with one object selected, the page; Page edge: the edges of the page; Page center: the center of the page; Grid: each object to the nearest line of the document grid. Click one of the six buttons: left edges, centers on a vertical line, right edges, top edges, centers on a horizontal line, or bottom edges. Use outline: align the outer edges of the outlines: with this on, the outer edges of the outlines meet, instead of the paths themselves. The keys always align to the object selected last: L Align Left R Align Right T Align Top B Align Bottom E Align Centers Horizontally C Align Centers Vertically P Center to Page Distributing Select three or more objects (two or more to distribute across the page). In the Distribute part, choose Distribute to: Selection extent (at first): the first and last objects stay where they are, and the others move between them; Page extent: the objects spread across the whole page, the first touching one side and the last the other. Click one of the eight buttons: left edges, centers, gaps or right edges across the page, or top edges, centers, gaps or bottom edges down it. Spreading the gaps gives equal space between the objects whatever their sizes. With too few objects the buttons are pale and the panel says how many are needed. Each align or distribute is one undo step. To place copies at even distances in one step, see Step and repeat. Fit objects to a path The Fit Objects to Path panel places objects along a line, a curve or the outline of a shape, with copies, spacing, placement and rotation of your choice. Select the objects, then the path last (Shift+click), and choose Object > Fit Objects to Path. See Fitting objects to a path for every setting.

h: Placing objects on a path The settings Objects and path Spacing Copies Placement Rotation Order Tips and limits
x: Fitting objects to a path The Fit Objects to Path panel places objects along a line, a curve or the outline of a shape: beads on a string, letters or stars round a seal, a row of fence posts along a road, dashes of your own along a border. It can make copies to fill the path, space them evenly or at a set distance, stand them on the path or turn them with it. Placing objects on a path Select the objects to place, then the path last (Shift+click). The panel shows how many objects are selected and what kind of object the path is. Choose Object > Fit Objects to Path to open the panel. Change the values you need (see below). Once a value changes, dashed outlines on the canvas show where every object and copy will go. Click Apply. Fitting undoes in one step. Copies go into the layer of the object they copy, with its fill, outline and effects. After an Apply that made copies, the objects placed and the copies are selected (not the path). The panel starts from the default values, with no outlines, each time you select other objects or work in another drawing; the values you enter stay while the same objects are selected. The settings The panel's groups, from top to bottom: Objects and path Keep originals (off): the selected objects stay where they are and copies of them are placed. Group all objects (off): what was placed goes into one group, which is selected. Treat subpaths as contiguous (on): a path made of several pieces is walked piece after piece, as one path. Off, only the first piece is used. Spacing Spacing: Evenly along the path (the default) spreads the objects over the whole path; Fixed distance puts them the Distance apart (10 mm at first). Measure between: between the Centers of neighbouring objects (the default) or between their Edges, so objects of different sizes get the same gap. Start offset (0): moves the first object along the path from its start. A negative value is allowed. End offset (0, open paths only): keeps the objects away from the end of the path. Place the row at (fixed distance only): puts the row at the Start (the default), in the Middle or at the End of the path. Copies Each object once (the default): each selected object is placed once. Number of objects (1 to 1000, 10 at first): that many objects in all: the selected ones, then copies of them in the same order. Fill the path (fixed distance only): as many as fit on the path. There are never more than 1000 objects in all. Placement Placement: On the path (the default), Above the path or Below the path, with a Distance from the path (0 at first) between the objects and the path. "Above" is on the left of the path's direction. Reference: the point of each object that goes on the path: its Center of rotation (the default; the centre, or where you moved it with the Pick tool), or a point of its Bounding box or Bounding box with outline. Origin (box references only): one of nine points of the box, picked in the grid (the centre at first). The bottom middle point makes the objects stand on the path. Rotation Rotation: Rotate objects to follow the path turns each object with the direction of the path; Fixed angle (the default) turns them all alike. The Angle (0, in degrees counterclockwise) is added in either case. Ignore initial rotation (off): straightens objects that were turned before they are placed. Under Modify rotation, the Style adds a turn to every object: None (the default): no extra turn. Uniform: every object turns by the Start angle. Progressive: each object turns a little more than the one before, the Spin angle (360 at first) times the Revolutions (1) over the whole row. Jitter: each object turns by a different amount, up to the Range (±) (15 degrees) either way. The same object turns the same way every time, in the preview and after Apply. Progressive jitter: both. Tick Clockwise to turn the other way. Only the fields the style uses can be changed. Order Order: which object goes first: As selected (the default), Reversed, Left to right, Right to left, Largest first, Smallest first, Large and small in turn, Top to bottom, Bottom to top, Tall to short, Short to tall, Wide to narrow, Narrow to wide or Random (shuffled the same way each time for the same objects). Reverse direction (off): starts from the other end of the path. Tips and limits On a closed shape the objects go all the way round, the closing side included, without the first and last meeting. On an open path, an object that would land past an end stays at that end. With more than 200 objects each one previews as its box; with more than 200 selected there is no preview, but Apply works. To place text along a path instead, see Adding and editing text. To spread objects in a straight row, see Aligning and distributing.

t: Making copies with Step and Repeat
h: To make copies
x: Making copies with Step and Repeat The Step and Repeat panel makes several copies of the selection, each moved by the same distance from the one before: a row of buttons, a column of lines, a grid of tiles. Open it with Edit > Step and Repeat (Ctrl+Shift+D).  To make copies Select the objects to copy. Set the number of Number of copies (1 to 999). Under Horizontal settings, choose how the copies are spaced across: Offset: the distance from one copy to the next, measured from the same point of each; Spacing: the gap between one copy and the next, so the copies never overlap whatever their size. Then type the distance. 0 keeps the copies in line. Do the same under Vertical settings. Click Apply. The copies are added to the active layer and selected. Distances are in the drawing units. The values stay as you typed them: after an Apply (the copies it made are selected) and for the next objects you select, the panel keeps the same number of copies, distances and modes until you change them. With nothing selected the fields wait, keeping their values. A new session starts from one copy, 6.35 mm across and 0 down. To copy with a rotation or a scale at each step, use the Copies field of the Transformations panel; see Moving, scaling, rotating and skewing.

h: The Objects panel Layers Master layers Renaming objects and layers Changing the order Grouping and combining Locking and hiding objects
x: Organizing objects and layers The Objects panel shows how the current page is organized: its layers, the objects on each layer, the groups and the master layers that appear on every page. Use it to select, name, hide, lock and order objects and layers. Objects higher in the list are drawn in front.  The Objects panel The panel lists the page with its layers, topmost first, then the Master Page with the master layers, the guidelines (Guides) and the Document Grid. Each object shows a thumbnail, the object itself drawn small with its fill and outline, and its name, or what it is when it has none ("Rectangle", "Curve with 8 nodes"). Click an object to select it; Shift+click adds it to the selection. Its layer becomes the active layer. Click the arrow of a group to see the objects inside it. Each layer has three buttons: Show/hide, Print and export the layer and Lock layer. A hidden or locked layer cannot be edited. The padlock of Guides locks all the guidelines of the page. Hidden objects show their name and thumbnail dimmed. To make the thumbnails larger or smaller, drag the slider between the small and the large square at the bottom of the panel, turn the mouse wheel over it, or hold Ctrl and turn the wheel over the list. The size is remembered. A thumbnail is drawn again only when its object changes, so long lists stay quick. Layers A layer is a sheet on which objects lie. The active layer, shown in bold with a colored bar, is where new objects go when you draw, paste, duplicate or import. Click a layer to make it active. New Layer, at the bottom of the panel, adds a layer on top and makes it active. Right-click a layer for Rename, Move up, Move down and Delete layer. A page always keeps one layer. Delete at the bottom of the panel deletes the selected objects, or the active layer when nothing is selected. Master layers Objects on a master layer appear on every page, under the page's own layers: use them for a logo, a header or page numbers. Click the New Master Layer (All Pages); right-click for odd or even pages button to add one for all pages; right-click it to add one for odd or even pages only. A master layer's menu has Show on to choose All pages, Odd pages or Even pages. You can select and edit master objects from any page they show on. Renaming objects and layers Double-click a layer or an object in the panel, or choose Rename from its menu, to open the Rename Layer or Rename Object dialog box. Type the new name and click OK. An object with an empty name shows what it is again. Double-click the page row to rename the page.  Names help you find objects in the panel and in Find and replace, and are kept in exported SVG files. Changing the order Object > Order moves the selected objects: To Front of Page, To Back of Page, To Front of Layer, To Back of Layer, Forward One, Back One, In Front Of, Behind (click the object to go in front of or behind) and Reverse Order. Grouping and combining Object > Group > Group (Ctrl+G) makes the selection one group that moves and resizes together. Ungroup (Ctrl+U) splits it again, and Ungroup All also splits the groups inside it. To edit an object inside a group without ungrouping, Ctrl+click it. Combine (Ctrl+L) makes the selected objects one curve of several parts, with one fill and outline; where the parts overlap, holes appear. Break Apart (Ctrl+K) splits a curve into its parts. Convert to Curves (Ctrl+Q) turns a rectangle, ellipse, polygon or text into a curve you can edit node by node. Locking and hiding objects Object > Lock > Lock Object keeps the selected objects from being selected or changed; Unlock Object and Unlock All Objects release them. Object > Hide > Hide Object hides the selected objects; Show All Objects shows them again. In the Objects panel every object's row has its own eye and padlock, to hide or show and lock or unlock it from the list, a locked object too. Selecting an object on the page scrolls the list to its row, so an object far down a long list comes into view. To keep objects out of the way while you work on others, see also Focus mode.

h: With objects selected With nothing selected
x: The Properties panel The Properties panel (Alt+Enter) shows and changes the properties of the selected objects: their outline, fill, transparency and more, depending on what is selected. It is open at first, beside Hints and Objects. Open it again with Object > Properties.  With objects selected The top of the panel names the selected object (and how many more are selected) and gives its position and size. Under it, a row of buttons opens and closes each section the object has: QR code, for a QR code: its content and look; see Barcodes and QR codes. Outline: color, width, paint, caps, corners, dashes, arrowheads and more; see Setting outlines. Fill: the kind of fill and its settings; see Fills. F11 opens this section. Transparency: how much of what lies below shows through; see Transparency. Rectangle, for rectangles: the corner settings; see Corners. FX: the bitmap effects applied to the object; see Bitmap effects. Character, for text: the font, size, Bold and Italic, and a button to Edit with the Text tool (F8). Summary: a summary of the object. The sections you closed stay closed the next time. A change applies to every selected object and is one undo step. With nothing selected With nothing selected, the panel says No objects selected and shows the Default properties for new objects: the fill and outline that new shapes and lines get. Change them here to draw with other colors from the start. See Object styles and defaults.

h: To place objects inside a frame Editing what is inside Opacity masks Empty frames
x: Placing objects inside a frame A clip frame is a closed object that holds other objects and shows only the parts of them that lie inside it, like a picture in a window. The frame keeps its own fill and outline; the objects inside stay whole and can be taken out again. The commands are in Object > Clip to Frame. To place objects inside a frame Select the objects to place inside. Choose Object > Clip to Frame > Place Inside Frame. Click the closed object that will be the frame. The objects keep their position. You can also drag the objects onto the frame with the right mouse button and choose to place them inside; see Dragging with the right button. Editing what is inside Edit Contents enters the frame: only the objects inside can be edited, the rest of the page is dimmed and the frame shows as an outline. Finish Editing Contents, or the button on the property bar, leaves it. Extract Contents makes the objects inside ordinary objects again; the frame stays, empty. Lock Contents to Frame (on at first): moving, scaling or rotating the frame takes the contents along. Turned off, the frame moves alone and the contents stay where they are on the page. Double-clicking a frame with the Pick tool, or Ctrl+click on it, also enters it, with the object under the pointer selected; see Focus mode. While you edit the contents, the dimmed objects outside the frame cannot be picked (by a click, a marquee, Select All or Tab). Undo stops at the start of the edit: undoing past it leaves the edit with the frame as it was; redo enters it again, and undoing Finish goes back into it. Opacity masks Object > Clip to Frame > Opacity Mask turns the selected clip frames into opacity masks: the frame is no longer drawn, and its brightness decides how much of the contents shows: fully where it is white, not at all where it is black, and nothing outside the frame. Fill the frame with a gradient for a soft fade. Invert Mask swaps that, so black shows. Choose the command again to turn the mask back into a plain frame. Empty frames Right-click an object and use its frame type commands: Create empty clip frame turns each selected object into an empty clip frame, ready to hold objects. No frame turns an empty clip frame back into the object it was. Create empty text frame replaces the object by an empty paragraph text frame of its size, ready for the Text tool. Cropping a bitmap with the Crop tool or the Shape tool also places it in a clip frame; see Cropping, cutting and erasing.

h: To create a symmetry Editing a symmetry Removing or keeping the copies
x: Drawing with symmetry Symmetry draws live mirrored copies of an object across one or more mirror lines. The copies follow every change you make to the original, so you draw one half (or one slice) and see the whole. The commands are in Object > Symmetry. To create a symmetry Select an object. Choose Object > Symmetry > Create New Symmetry (Alt+S). A vertical mirror line is placed at the right edge of the object, so the copy appears next to it, and TraceDraw goes straight into editing the symmetry. Editing a symmetry Edit Symmetry (Alt+E) edits the symmetry of the selected object. A bar at the top left of the drawing window sets: the number of mirror lines, 1 to 12, spread evenly around the center. With more lines you get a kaleidoscope: with n lines there are 2*n* - 1 copies; the center (X and Y); the angle of the first line (0 to 360 degrees); Show full preview (copies drawn in full, or as red outlines when off) and Show symmetry lines. Edit the originals as usual, with any tool; the copies follow. A click or a marquee picks one of the originals inside the symmetry, and objects you draw, paste or duplicate join it. Drag a mirror line with the Pick tool to move the lines; click a line to show round handles at its ends and drag one to turn the lines. While an object with symmetry is selected or edited, its mirror lines show as dashed lines. Click Finish on the bar, or choose Finish Editing Symmetry (Alt+Shift+E), to stop editing. Removing or keeping the copies Remove Symmetry (Alt+Shift+S) removes the symmetry; the copies go away. Break Symmetry Link (Alt+X) turns the copies into objects of their own, which no longer follow the original.

h: Entering and leaving focus mode While in focus mode Settings
x: Focus mode Focus mode lets you edit the objects inside a group or a clip frame without ungrouping it, with the rest of the drawing faded behind it. Entering and leaving focus mode Double-click a group or a clip frame with the Pick tool. Or right-click an object and choose Bring into focus. For an object inside a group, the group gets the focus and the object stays selected. Double-click a group inside the focused group to go one level deeper. Press Esc with nothing selected to go up one level, and leave focus mode from the top. The cross on the breadcrumb bar leaves at once. While in focus mode A bar at the top left of the drawing window shows the name of the drawing, then each group on the way down. Click a step to go back to that group, or the name of the drawing to leave focus mode. Clicks and marquees select the objects inside the focused group, so you can move, color or delete them with the Pick tool as usual. Everything else is faded. Exports and printing are not affected. Settings How faded the other objects are is set by the visibility of inactive objects (0 to 100%, 20% at first) on the Edit page of Tools > Options > TraceDraw. Whether a double-click enters focus mode is set on the same page. See TraceDraw options.

h: Making a symbol Placing instances Turning instances back into objects
x: Symbols A symbol is an object you define once and place many times. Each copy, called an instance, is a link to the definition: edit the definition and every instance changes. Symbols keep files small and repeated parts the same. They are listed in the Symbols panel (Ctrl+F3).  Making a symbol Select the objects that make up the symbol. Click New symbol from selection in the Symbols panel, or choose Object > Symbol > New Symbol or Object > Create > Symbol. The selection becomes the first instance of the new symbol. Placing instances The panel lists the symbols of the drawing, each with the number of its instances. Click Insert beside a symbol to place a new instance, or choose Object > Symbol > Insert Symbol. Instances can be moved, scaled and turned like any object. An instance copied in one drawing and pasted in another brings its symbol along (and the symbols it shows), so it shows the same objects there. Pasting again reuses the symbol already brought. Turning instances back into objects Select instances and click Revert to objects, or choose Object > Symbol > Revert to Objects. They become ordinary objects that no longer follow the symbol.

h: Adding and editing data
x: Object data The Object Data panel attaches your own information to an object, as named fields: a part number, a price, a note. The data is saved with the drawing and goes with the object when you copy it.  Adding and editing data Select an object. With nothing selected, the panel says Select an object.. The panel lists the object's fields in two columns, Field and Value. Click a name or a value to edit it. Click Add field to add a field, or one of the buttons for a common field: Name, Cost, Comments and CDRStaticID. Click the x at the end of a row to remove the field. When the selected objects have a Cost field with a number, the panel shows their total cost. Some features keep their own data in objects, such as dimension lines, callouts, connectors and anchors; you rarely need to change those fields by hand.

h: To add a link Bookmarks Links in exported files
x: Links and bookmarks The Links and Bookmarks panel gives objects a hyperlink, so a click on them in an exported PDF, SVG or web page opens a web address, writes an email or goes to another page. It also lists the named objects of the drawing as bookmarks. Open it from Window > Panels.  To add a link Select one or more objects. Type the address in the Hyperlink field and leave the field. The buttons Web, E-mail and Page put https://, mailto: or #page= in front of the text, so for a page link you only type its number. Click Remove to take a link away, or empty the field. Bookmarks Under Bookmarks (named objects), the panel lists one button per object that has a name. Click one to select the object and zoom to it. To name objects, see Renaming objects and layers. Links in exported files In PDF files, each linked object becomes a clickable area over its box. A page link goes to the top of that page of the file. PDF/X files get no links, as those standards do not allow them. In SVG and web pages, the object itself is the link. A link on a group covers all its objects; the links of the objects inside are left out.

h: To paste in another form
x: Paste Special Edit > Paste Special chooses how the content of the clipboard comes into the drawing, when it could come in more than one way: for example text copied from another program can become a text object, and an SVG copied from a web page can become editable shapes or a picture.  To paste in another form Copy something, in TraceDraw or in another program. Choose Edit > Paste Special. Under Paste as, choose one of the forms the clipboard offers: Objects (internal clipboard): objects copied in TraceDraw, as they were; Vector objects (SVG text): SVG text, turned into shapes you can edit; Bitmap: an image, as a bitmap; Artistic text: plain text, as a line of text. Click OK. When the clipboard holds nothing that can be pasted, the dialog box says The clipboard is empty. The ordinary Paste (Ctrl+V) pastes in the first form available, and Paste in View (Ctrl+Shift+V) pastes in the middle of the window.

h: Adding to the Shelf Placing an item Arranging items Removing an item Where the Shelf is kept
x: The Shelf The Shelf panel keeps objects and colors apart from any drawing, so you can place them in this drawing or another one, today or after TraceDraw restarts: logos, stamps, frames, a set of colors. Open it from Window > Panels, or right-click a selection and choose Add to Shelf.  Adding to the Shelf Select objects and click Add Selection. The item is named after the object (its name, or what it is), or "n objects". Symbols become plain objects, and the object styles they use go along. Click Add Colours to keep the colors of the drawing's document palette and its color styles as one item. The Shelf holds up to 500 items. Placing an item Drag an item onto the drawing to place a copy under the pointer. Double-click an item, or choose it and click Place, to place a copy in the middle of the view. The copies go on the active layer and are selected; one undo removes them. A color item adds its colors to the document palette and its color styles to the drawing. Arranging items Click an item to choose it. Right-click it for Place, Rename and Remove. Drag an item onto another to move it to that place. Removing an item Choose an item and click Remove. Removing cannot be undone, so TraceDraw asks first: click Remove to confirm or Cancel to keep it. Tick Do not ask again to remove items without asking; to be asked again, turn on Before an item is removed from the Shelf on the Warnings page of the global options.  Where the Shelf is kept On the desktop, the Shelf is a file in your preferences folder. In the browser, it is kept in that browser's storage, which holds only a few megabytes, so large bitmaps may not be kept.

h: Finding and replacing text Finding objects Finding and replacing by properties
x: Finding and replacing The Find and Replace panel (Ctrl+F) finds text in the drawing, and replaces it, finds objects by name, or finds objects by their fill, outline, outline width, font or type and replaces those. Open it with Edit > Find and Replace.  Finding and replacing text Choose Text. Type what to look for in Find, and the new text in Replace with. Tick Match case to tell capitals from small letters, and Whole words only to skip the text when it is part of a longer word. Click Find Next to select the next text object that holds it, or Find All to select them all. Click Replace to replace it in the selected text, or Replace All to replace it everywhere. The panel says how many were found. Finding objects Choose Objects, type part of a name, or a kind of object such as "Rectangle", and click Find Next or Find All. The search covers the current page. To name objects, see Renaming objects and layers. Finding and replacing by properties Choose Properties. In Look in, choose This page or Whole drawing. Under Find objects with, tick what to look for: Type, Fill, Outline (a colour, or None), Outline width or Font. An object is found when it has everything ticked. From Selection takes these from the selected object, for example to find every object filled with its colour. Click Previous or Find Next to select the objects one by one (on other pages too), or Find All to select those on this page. To change them, tick under Replace with the new fill colour, outline colour, outline width or font, and click Replace All. All the changes undo in one step. A fill colour looked for is replaced wherever it is used, in gradients too. Locked objects are left as they are. For every option, how colors are compared and what each replacement does, see Finding and replacing by properties.

h: Finding objects Replacing properties How objects are compared
x: Finding and replacing by properties The Properties mode of the Find and Replace panel finds objects by how they look and what they are: every object filled with one red, every outline 0.2 mm wide, every text in a font you no longer want, every bitmap. It then selects them, or changes their fill, outline or font all at once. Finding objects Choose Edit > Find and Replace (Ctrl+F) and click Properties. In Look in, choose This page (the default) or Whole drawing (every page, then the master layers). Under Find objects with, tick what to look for. An object is found when it has everything ticked: Type (off; Rectangle at first): only objects of one kind: Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon or star, Curve, Artistic text, Paragraph text, Group, Bitmap, Clip frame, Table or Symbol. Fill (on; black at first): objects filled with this color, as a uniform fill or in a gradient or mesh fill, or None for objects without a fill. Outline (off): objects whose outline has this color, or None for objects without an outline. Outline width (off; 0.2 mm at first, in the outline unit): objects whose outline has this width. Font (off): text that uses this font family, in any mix of capitals and small letters. To look for what an object has, select it and click From Selection: its fill color (or none), outline color (or none), outline width and font fill the fields, ticked where it makes sense (the width and the type stay unticked). Reset clears everything back to the defaults. Click a button: Previous or Find Next selects the objects found one at a time, going round at the end. With Whole drawing, the page of each object comes into view. Find All selects every object found on the current page. The status bar says how many were found in all and how many on this page. The panel shows the number of objects found. Replacing properties Find the objects as above. Under Replace with, tick what to change and set the new value: Fill: when a fill color is looked for, that color is replaced by the new one wherever it is used, in gradients and mesh fills too; otherwise the objects get a uniform fill of the new color. Outline: when an outline color is looked for, outlines of that color take the new one; otherwise every outline does. Objects without an outline stay without one. Outline width: every outline of the objects found takes the new width. Font: when a font is looked for, text in that font takes the new one; otherwise all the text of the objects found does. Click Replace All. All the changes undo in one step. The status bar says in how many objects something changed. Locked objects, and objects on locked layers, are found but left as they are. How objects are compared Colors count as the same when they are in the same model with every value within half a percent, or, in different models, when they show as the same color on screen. A spot color matches the same ink at the same tint, and the registration color matches only itself. Widths count as the same within half a thousandth of a millimetre. In groups and clip frames, the objects inside are checked at any depth, and the group is found when one of them matches. With only Type ticked, the group's own type counts. Only objects at the top level are selected, since those are what you can select. To find text or names instead, see Finding and replacing.

h: Adding a comment Reading and answering
x: Comments The Comments panel collects review notes on a drawing: pins, boxes and arrows on the page, each with a text and replies. Comments are saved with the drawing (in .tdraw files) and are never printed or exported. Open the panel from Window > Panels.  Adding a comment Type your name in Name. It signs your comments and replies. Left empty, the author of the drawing is used. Next to Add, click Pin, Box or Arrow. On the page, click to place a pin, or drag to draw a box around something or an arrow pointing at it. Type the comment. Each comment shows its number in an orange bubble on the page. Reading and answering The panel lists the comments, with how many are open, each with its number, author, date and time, page, text and replies. Click a card to choose the comment and go to its page; with the panel open, you can also click a bubble or a box on the page. Edit the text of the chosen comment, or type in the Reply field and press Enter or click Reply. Resolve marks a comment as dealt with; Reopen opens it again. Resolved comments are hidden unless Show resolved is ticked. Hide marks hides the bubbles, boxes and arrows on the page. Delete removes a comment and its replies. Every change is one undo step. Deleting a page deletes its comments.

h: Creating a table Typing in cells Changing rows and columns Converting text and tables
x: Tables A table is an object made of rows and columns of cells, each of which can hold text and a fill. Draw tables with the Table tool and change them with the Table menu. Creating a table Choose Table > Create New Table (or Object > Create > New Table). In the Create New Table dialog box, set the Number of Rows, the Number of Columns and the height and width (100 by 75 mm at first), and click OK. The table is placed in the middle of the page and selected. Or choose the Table tool and drag a rectangle: the table fills it, with equal rows and columns.  On the property bar of the Table tool, set the number of rows (3 at first) and columns (4 at first), the cell fill (none at first), and the border width and color. With a table selected, the fill and border change that table; otherwise they apply to the next table you draw. Typing in cells With the Table tool, click a cell and type. Text editing works as in any text: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+U format the selected characters, or the whole cell. Enter adds a line, Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and previous cell, and the arrow keys step to the next cell at the edge of the text. A row grows when its text needs more height. Shift+click adds cells to the selection. Changing rows and columns The Table menu acts on the active cell and the selected cells: Insert: Row Above, Row Below, Column Left and Column Right. The new row or column takes the size of its neighbour. Select: Cell, Row, Column or Table. Delete: Row, Column or Table. A table keeps at least one row and one column. Distribute: Rows Evenly or Columns Evenly, keeping the size of the table. Merge Cells (Ctrl+M) makes the selected cells one cell, with their texts in order; Unmerge Cells splits it again, keeping the text and fill in the top left cell. Split into Rows and Split into Columns split the active row or column into two halves. Converting text and tables Convert Text to Table: each paragraph of the selected text becomes a row. The dialog box asks what separates the cells: commas, tabs, nothing (each paragraph is one cell, in one column) or characters of your own under User defined, and tells how many rows and columns the table will have. It starts with tabs when the text has any, else commas when it has any. The spaces around each cell's text are left out, so "Anna, Ben, Carl" with commas makes three cells. Convert Table to Text: the cells are joined by tabs and the rows by line breaks. The defaults of the tool are on the Table page of the tool options; see Tool options.

h: Making a barcode Step 1: the standard and the data Step 2: printer and sizes Step 3: the text QR codes
x: Barcodes and QR codes TraceDraw makes barcodes for products, labels and inventory, and QR codes that phones can read. Both are made of ordinary vector shapes, so they print sharp at any size. Making a barcode Choose Object > Insert > Barcode to open the Barcode Wizard. It has three steps; a Sample preview under each shows the barcode as it will be made. Use Next and Back to move between steps, and Finish on the last one.  Step 1: the standard and the data Choose one of the standards and type the data. Choosing a standard puts a sample in the field, and the wizard says what the standard accepts: Codabar: up to 30 digits and the signs - $ : / . +, between start and stop characters A to D. Code 39: capital letters, digits and - . space $ / + %. Code 128: any printable character. EAN-13, EAN-8 and UPC-A: 12, 7 or 11 digits, or one more with the check digit, optionally followed by a space and a 2- or 5-digit add-on. UPC-E: 6 digits, or the number system (0 or 1) and 6 digits. Interleaved 2 of 5: up to 40 digits. Data the standard cannot hold keeps you on this step with a message. Step 2: printer and sizes Printer: the resolution of the printer, 150 to 2400 dpi (300 at first). Bars are made a whole number of printer dots wide, so they print evenly. Units for the sizes below. Bar width reduction: printer dots taken off every bar to make up for ink spreading (1 at first). The barcode keeps its width. Magnification (scale): 100% is the standard size. Bar height (1 inch at first), with the resulting Symbol width: {w}. Wide to narrow: 2.0 to 3.0, for Codabar, Code 39 and Interleaved 2 of 5. Advanced adds Add the check character (Code 39 and Interleaved 2 of 5) and the Quiet zone, a white margin behind the bars in modules. Step 3: the text The Font, Size (12 points at first), Weight and Alignment of the readable text. Options, available where the standard uses them: Center sys/check, Place text above, Show add-on text, Add-on text at bottom, Show FACT data, Show asterisks, Show quiet zone marks and Show start/stop. Make this bar code human readable (show text): turn it off for bars without text. Finish places the barcode in the middle of the page as one group and selects it. QR codes Choose Object > Insert > QR Code. A QR code is placed in the middle of the page at once, and the Properties panel opens at its QR Code section: Choose the kind of content: URL, Email, Phone number, SMS, Contact (vCard), Text or Location. Fill in its fields, such as Address (URL), or First name, Last name, Phone number and Email address for a contact. A field applies when you leave it. Fields the kinds share are kept when you change the kind. Set the look: Pixel fill and Background fill (any fill), Pixel outline and Pixel size (2.5 mm at first). Click Validate to check that the code reads back. A green message says it does; a red one says why not, for example when the pixels are not dark enough against the background. The QR code stays editable: move, scale or turn it as any object and change its content later. To make it plain shapes, ungroup it. Content that cannot be encoded, or too much of it, changes nothing and shows in red.

Barvy, výplně a průhlednosti Každý objekt může mít uvnitř výplň a podél okraje obrys. Tyto stránky vysvětlují, jak vybírat barvy z palet a panelu Barva, druhy výplní (jednolitá barva, přechod, vzorek, textura nebo síť), jak objekty zprůhlednit a jak udržet barvy jednotné pomocí barevných stylů, přímých barev a správy barev.

h: Výběr barvy Nabrání barvy Přímé barvy
x: Panel Barva Panel Barva (Shift+F11) namíchá barvu a použije ji na výplň nebo obrys výběru. Otevře jej také nástroj Barva obrysu (Shift+F12). Otevřete jej z nabídky Okno > Panely.  Výběr barvy Vyberte objekty. Panel začne barvou výplně prvního z nich. Novou barvu namíchejte v jednom ze zobrazení: Zobrazení barev: kliknutím nebo tažením ve čtverci nastavíte sytost (zleva doprava) a jas (zdola nahoru) a v pruhu vedle něj odstín; Barevné posuvníky: jeden posuvník pro každou složku nastavení Model: RGB, CMYK (výchozí), HSB, HSL, Lab, stupně šedi nebo YIQ; Barevné palety: vzorky barev palety. Tři tlačítka nahoře zobrazují nebo skrývají jednotlivá zobrazení; zobrazit lze libovolnou kombinaci. Můžete také zadat hodnotu #rrggbb. Kliknutím na Výplň nebo Obrys dole v panelu novou barvu použijete. Zámek (Zamknout výplň a obrys) spojuje výplň a obrys, takže kterékoli z tlačítek použije barvu na obojí. Tlačítko "..." (Další akce) rozbalí další akce: Bez výplně, Bez obrysu, Prohodit barvy, Přidat do palety dokumentu, Přidat k vlastním přímým barvám a Přidat do palety stylů barev. Stará a nová barva se zobrazují vedle sebe. Pokud novou barvu nelze přesně vytisknout barvami CMYK, panel zobrazí upozornění. Nabrání barvy Klikněte na Kapátko a pak kamkoli do kresby a naberete barvu z tohoto místa. Poté kliknutím na Použít vzorkovanou barvu {c} z ní uděláte novou barvu. Viz také Kapátka. Přímé barvy Pod tlačítky Přímé barvy uvádí přímé barvy kresby; viz Přímé barvy.

h: Používání palety Paleta dokumentu Panel Palety Úprava palety
x: Barevné palety Barevná paleta podél spodního okraje okna je nejrychlejší způsob, jak obarvovat objekty. Pod ní paleta dokumentu shromažďuje barvy, které kresba používá. Můžete otevřít další palety, vytvářet vlastní a upravovat je. Používání palety Kliknutí na barvu vyplní výběr (když není nic vybráno, nastaví výplň nových objektů) Kliknutí pravým tlačítkem na barvu obarví obrys výběru Ctrl+kliknutí na barvu přimíchá desetinu barvy do výplně výběru Kliknutí a podržení barvy nabídne světlejší, tmavší, matnější a jasnější odstíny Přetažení barvy na objekt vyplní objekt, nebo obarví jeho obrys, je-li puštěna na okraj Kliknutí na přeškrtnuté pole odebere výplň (pravým tlačítkem: obrys) Šipky na koncích paletu posouvají a tlačítko na pravém konci zobrazí všechny barvy najednou. Když na barvu najedete ukazatelem, uvidíte její název a hodnoty. Tlačítko nabídky palety na levém konci otevře nabídku palety. Paletu lze přesunout k jinému okraji okna nebo ji nechat plovoucí: táhněte ji za tečkovaný úchyt. Paleta dokumentu Každá barva, kterou použijete na objekt, se přidá do palety dokumentu, která se ukládá s kresbou. Její kapátko přidá barvu pod ukazatelem a její nabídka obsahuje Automaticky aktualizovat (pro vypnutí samočinného přidávání barev), Přidat z výběru, Přidat z dokumentu, Odstranit barvu a Obnovit paletu (ponechá jen barvy, které kresba stále používá). Můžete na ni také přetahovat barvy nebo objekty. Jak ji zobrazit nebo skrýt, viz Možnosti přizpůsobení. Panel Palety Panel Palety uvádí palety, které máte, s počtem barev v každé. Otevřete jej příkazem Okno > Barevné palety > Správce palet.  Zaškrtnutím paletu zobrazíte pod oknem kresby. Upravit ji otevře v editoru palet. Otevřít paletu otevře soubor palety (.tdpal, .gpl, .ase nebo .aco). Vytvořit paletu z dokumentu a Vytvořit paletu z výběru vytvoří paletu z barev použitých v kresbě nebo ve výběru. Barvy palety dokumentu jsou zobrazeny dole; kliknutím na jednu vyplníte výběr, kliknutím pravým tlačítkem obarvíte obrys. Úprava palety Okno > Barevné palety > Editor palet otevře editor palet.  Zvolte paletu k úpravě v poli Paleta, nebo kliknutím na Nová začněte novou. Zadejte její Název. Kliknutím na barvu ji vyberete; Přidat barvu přidá aktuální barvu a Odebrat barvu odebere vybranou. Kliknutím na Uložit paletu ji uložíte jako soubor. Klikněte na Zavřít. Vestavěné palety nelze upravovat; vytvořte novou paletu nebo upravte kopii.

h: Způsoby vyplnění objektu Jednotné výplně Přechodové výplně Dialog Upravit výplň Nástroj Interaktivní výplň Nástroj Výplň oblasti Síťové výplně Vzorkové a texturové výplně Více výplní na jednom objektu
x: Výplně Výplň barví vnitřek uzavřeného objektu. TraceDraw má šest druhů výplně: Žádná, Jednotná (jedna plná barva), Přechod (barvy, které do sebe plynule přecházejí), Vzorek, Textura a Síť (barvy plynoucí mezi uzly mřížky). Způsoby vyplnění objektu Kliknutím na barvu v paletě dáte výběru jednotnou výplň. Použijte oddíl Výplň panelu Vlastnosti (F11): řadou obrázků zvolte druh výplně a poté její nastavení. Nástrojem Interaktivní výplň (G) nastavíte přechody přímo na objektu. Nástrojem Výplň oblasti vyplníte oblast ohraničenou několika objekty. Nástrojem Síťová výplň (M) vytvoříte síťovou výplň. Když není nic vybráno, zvolená výplň se stane výplní nových objektů. Jednotné výplně Jednotná výplň je jedna barva v libovolném barevném modelu. Zvolte ji z palety, z panelu Barva (viz Panel Barva) nebo z oddílu výplně panelu Vlastnosti. Přechodové výplně Přechod prolíná dvě nebo více barev. Jeho nastavení v oddílu výplně panelu Vlastnosti: Typ: Lineární (podél přímky), Radiální (od středu ven), Kuželový (kolem středu), Čtvercový (ve zvětšujících se čtvercích) nebo Shaped (podle obrysu objektu, od okraje dovnitř). Gradients: hotové přechody, ze kterých lze vyjít. Zarážky: barvy a jejich místa podél přechodu, 2 až 64. Vyberte zarážku a změňte její barvu nebo polohu; Přidat zarážku a Odebrat zarážku zarážky přidávají a odebírají. Importovat přechod převezme barvy ze souboru přechodu .ggr. Úhel lineárních, kuželových a čtvercových přechodů, okrajová rezerva (jak velká část každého konce je plnou barvou) a posun středu radiálních, kuželových a čtvercových přechodů. Repeat: None, Sawtooth (barvy běží znovu od začátku) nebo Mirror (běží tam a zpět), s počtem opakování Cycles. Bilinear: barvy běží od první k poslední a zpět. Invert colours: barvy běží v obráceném pořadí. Pruh pod typem ukazuje celý průběh barev tak, jak se vykreslí. Dialog Upravit výplň F11 otevře dialog Edit Fill s výplní výběru. U přechodu ukazuje náhled, Fill picker, typ, opakování a pás barev: klepnutím uzel vyberete, tažením posunete, poklepáním uzel přidáte nebo odstraníte. Pod pásem je barva, průhlednost, poloha a Midpoint uzlu a Reverse. Transform obsahuje otočení, střed a okraj. OK použije, co jste změnili, i s Overprint fill. Dokud je dialogové okno otevřené, výběr ukazuje výplň průběžně při změnách; Zrušit nebo Esc vrátí původní výplň.  Nástroj Interaktivní výplň Nástroj Interaktivní výplň (G) upravuje výplně přímo na objektu. Zvolte nástroj a táhněte přes objekt: vznikne lineární přechod od místa stisknutí k místu uvolnění. Podržením Ctrl omezíte úhel na kroky po 15 stupních. Kliknutí dá výchozí výplň. Tažením uzlů na objektu přechod měníte: dva čtvercové uzly lineárního přechodu mění jeho směr a délku; uzel radiálního, kuželového nebo čtvercového přechodu posouvá jeho střed. Přetažením barvy z palety na uzel jej přebarvíte, přetažením na čáru mezi uzly tam přidáte barvu. Lišta vlastností obsahuje druh výplně a jeho nastavení: barvu jednotné výplně; u přechodu typ, počáteční a koncovou barvu, úhel a okrajovou rezervu. Nástroj Výplň oblasti Nástroj Výplň oblasti vyplní libovolnou uzavřenou oblast, i takovou, kterou tvoří několik překrývajících se objektů, tím, že z této oblasti vytvoří nový objekt. Okolní objekty zůstanou, jak jsou. Zvolte nástroj Výplň oblasti. Na liště vlastností zvolte výplň a obrys: Použít výchozí (výplň a obrys nových objektů; je-li to žádná výplň, použije se barva, aby byla oblast vidět), Určit (barva a u obrysu vedle ní šířka) nebo Žádná. Klikněte dovnitř oblasti. Nový objekt se umístí navrch aktivní vrstvy a je vybraný. Kliknutí na obrys nebo do oblasti, kterou nic neohraničuje, nic nevytvoří. Síťové výplně Síťová výplň je mřížka uzlů přes objekt, každý uzel s vlastní barvou a průhledností; barvy mezi uzly plynule přecházejí. Hodí se pro realistické stínování. Zvolte nástroj Síťová výplň (M) a na liště vlastností nastavte řádky a sloupce (výchozí 2 x 2, nejvýše 50). Klikněte na objekt. Dostane síť v barvě své výplně. Kliknutím na uzel jej vyberete, kliknutím na barvu v paletě jej obarvíte. Tažením uzlů ohýbáte tok barev. Dvojitým kliknutím uvnitř sítě přidáte řádek nebo sloupec procházející nejbližším uzlem; vyberte uzel a stisknutím Delete odeberete jeho řádek a sloupec. Lišta vlastností obsahuje také Vyhlazenou barvu, která barvy prolíná jemněji, průhlednost vybraného uzlu a Zrušit síť, které síťovou výplň odebere. Změna řádků a sloupců sítě zachová její barvy. Vzorkové a texturové výplně Výplň Vzorek opakuje dlaždici: dvoubarevnou, vektorový vzorek nebo bitmapu. Viz Vzorkové výplně. Výplň Textura je generovaná, přirozeně působící textura: Mraky, Mramor, Šum nebo Dřevo, s vlastními barvami a měřítkem. Více výplní na jednom objektu V oddílu výplně panelu Vlastnosti přidá Přidat výplň přes vlastní výplň objektu další výplň, která začíná jako kopie k úpravě. Další výplně se zobrazují jako „Výplň 2“, „Výplň 3“ a tak dále, každá s vlastním editorem a tlačítkem pro odebrání. Oddíl obrysu může stejným způsobem přidávat další obrysy. Výplně lze malovat i na obrysy; viz Nastavení obrysů.

h: Vytvoření vzorku z vlastních objektů Nastavení vzorku Vzorky v exportovaných souborech
x: Vzorkové výplně Vzorková výplň opakuje dlaždici po celém vnitřku objektu. Dlaždice může být dvoubarevná, sada vektorových objektů (plnobarevný vektorový vzorek) nebo bitmapa. Dlaždice jsou ukotveny ke stránce, takže se při posunu objektu neposouvají. Vytvoření vzorku z vlastních objektů Nakreslete objekty, které tvoří jednu dlaždici, a vyberte je. Zvolte Objekt > Vytvořit > Vzorová výplň. V dialogovém okně Vytvořit vzorek zvolte Typ: Vektorový ponechá objekty jako vektory, ostré v jakékoli velikosti; Bitmapa z nich vytvoří obrázek. Klikněte na OK.  Vzorek se stane výplní nových objektů. Chcete-li jej dát již nakresleným objektům, zvolte Vzorek v oddílu výplně panelu Vlastnosti. Nastavení vzorku V oddílu výplně panelu Vlastnosti zvolte Vzorek, poté druh vzorku a jeho nastavení. U vektorového vzorku panel ukazuje, kolik objektů dlaždice obsahuje, a její šířku a výšku: jejich změnou se spolu s nimi změní velikost obsahu dlaždice. Vzorky v exportovaných souborech Soubory SVG uchovávají vektorové vzorky jako vektory. Soubory PDF a EPS je dostanou jako obrázky v rozlišení exportu, oříznuté podle objektu.

h: Kapátko barev Kapátko atributů
x: Kopírování barev a atributů kapátky Nástroje kapátka naberou barvu nebo celou sadu atributů z jednoho objektu a předají je jiným. Oba pracují ve dvou krocích, zobrazených na liště vlastností: vybrat (nabrat vzorek) a použít (malovat jím). Po nabrání vzorku se nástroj přepne na použití; dalším vzorkem začnete kliknutím na tlačítko výběru. Esc vzorek zahodí a vrátí se k nástroji Výběr. Ukazatel je kapátko, když nástroj odebírá vzorek, a kbelík s barvou, když ho používá. Obrázky dávají svou barvu i ve skupině nebo v rámečku. Kapátko barev Zvolte nástroj Kapátko barev. Kliknutím na objekt naberete jeho barvu: barvu jednotné výplně, první barvu přechodu nebo barvu obrysu. Na bitmapě nabere barvu pixelů pod ukazatelem, zprůměrovanou přes velikost vzorku nastavenou na liště vlastností (1 x 1, 2 x 2 nebo 5 x 5 pixelů). Shift+kliknutí nabere přednostně barvu obrysu. Kliknutím na objekty je vyplníte touto barvou; Shift+kliknutím obarvíte jejich obrys (objekt bez obrysu dostane tenký obrys). Kliknutím dovnitř prázdného uzavřeného tvaru jej vyplníte. Lišta vlastností ukazuje nabranou barvu. Když pohybujete ukazatelem, abyste vzali barvu, malé pole vedle něj ukazuje barvu pod ním: vzorek, název barvy, je-li to barva palety nebo přímá barva, její hodnoty v barevném režimu kresby (CMYK nebo RGB) a její hexadecimální hodnotu. Kapátko výběru barvy ukazuje totéž pole. Kapátko atributů Nástroj Kapátko atributů kopíruje několik vlastností najednou z jednoho objektu na jiné. Zvolte nástroj Kapátko atributů. Na liště vlastností zvolte, co se má kopírovat: Vlastnosti: obrys, výplň a text (písmo, velikost a styl; samotný text zůstane). Výchozí vše zapnuto. Transformace: velikost, otočení a poloha. Výchozí vypnuto. Efekty: průhlednost, vržený stín a živé efekty. Výchozí vypnuto. Klikněte na objekt, ze kterého se kopíruje. Klikněte na každý objekt, na který se kopíruje. Shift+kliknutí místo toho nabere vzorek z jiného objektu. Každé kliknutí je jeden krok zpět.

h: Vytváření barevných stylů Používání a úprava stylů Harmonie
x: Barevné styly Barevný styl je pojmenovaná barva, kterou používají objekty kresby. Když styl změníte, změní se i každý objekt, který je jím vyplněn. Barvy návrhu tak zůstanou jednotné a rychle vyzkoušíte jiná barevná schémata. Styly jsou uvedeny v panelu Barevné styly; otevřete jej z nabídky Okno > Panely.  Vytváření barevných stylů Nový z výběru přidá styl pro každou barvu výplně vybraných objektů, která ještě není stylem. Nový barevný styl přidá styl z aktuální barvy panelu Barva. Používání a úprava stylů Každý styl zobrazuje svou barvu, název a tři tlačítka: kliknutím na barvu ji změníte: objekty vyplněné touto barvou se přizpůsobí; kliknutím na název jej přejmenujete; Výplň vyplní výběr stylem, Obrys obarví jeho obrys; x styl odebere (objekty si svou barvu ponechají). Harmonie Editor harmonií vytvoří sadu stylů, které k sobě ladí, ze základní barvy Základní barva: Zvolte Základní barva. Klikněte na harmonii: Analogická, Komplementární, Rozdělená komplementární, Triadická, Tetradická nebo Monochromatická. Barvy harmonie se přidají jako styly pojmenované podle ní.

h: Použití průhlednosti Nastavení
x: Průhlednost Průhlednost nechá prosvítat to, co leží pod objektem. Může být všude stejná, měnit se napříč objektem jako přechod, nebo sledovat vzorek či texturu. Použití průhlednosti Nástrojem Průhlednost: klikněte na objekt a pak na liště vlastností zvolte druh průhlednosti, nebo táhněte přes objekt a vznikne přechodová průhlednost od neprůhledné (kde stisknete) po průhlednou (kde uvolníte). Uzly přechodu se pak ukážou na objektu jako u nástroje Interaktivní výplň: táhněte začátek, konec nebo kulatý uzel zkosení; tažením příčky mezi dvěma uzly (středový bod) posunete místo, kde je přechod v polovině; dvojklik na čáru přidá uzel, na uzel ho odebere. V oddílu Průhlednost panelu Vlastnosti. Nastavení Druh: Bez průhlednosti, Jednotná (výchozí), Přechod (lineární, radiální, kuželový, čtvercový nebo tvarovaný, jako u přechodových výplní), Vzorek nebo Textura. Míra: 0 až 100 % (výchozí 50 %). U přechodu jsou zarážky odstíny šedi: bílá je neprůhledná, černá zcela průhledná. Režim slučování: jak se barvy mísí s tím, co leží pod nimi. Normální (výchozí) jednoduše prosvítá; ostatní, například Přidat, Odečíst, Rozdíl, Násobit, Dělit, Je-li světlejší, Je-li tmavší, Odstín, Sytost, Barva a Invertovat, kombinují barvy jinými způsoby. Zda se týká možnosti Výplň, Obrys nebo Vše. Zmrazit: zachová to, co prosvítá, v současné podobě, i když se objekty pod ním posunou. Chcete-li zkopírovat průhlednost jiného objektu, použijte Objekt > Kopírovat efekt > Průhlednost z. O průhledných oblastech určených jasem objektu viz Masky neprůhlednosti.

h: Přidání přímé barvy Používání přímých barev Vzorníky barev Přímé barvy v tisku a exportech
x: Přímé barvy Přímá barva je pojmenovaná tisková barva, která se tiskne z vlastní desky, například metalická nebo firemní barva, místo aby se míchala z azurové, purpurové, žluté a černé. Každá kresba si vede seznam svých přímých barev. Každá barva má náhradu složenou z procesních barev, která slouží k jejímu zobrazení na obrazovce a všude, kde přímou barvu nelze použít. Přidání přímé barvy Otevřete panel Barva a namíchejte barvu, jak má přímá barva vypadat. Pod Přímé barvy zadejte Název barvy. Klikněte na Nová přímá barva. Názvy jsou v rámci kresby jedinečné. Používání přímých barev Seznam Přímé barvy ukazuje každou barvu se vzorkem, jejím názvem a tlačítky Výplň a Obrys, která ji použijí na výběr v nastaveném odstínu Tón (0 až 100 %, výchozí 100 %). Křížek na konci řádku barvu ze seznamu odebere; objekty, které ji používají, si ponechají její náhradní barvu. Vzorníky barev Soubor palety může být vzorníkem přímých barev (například paleta .ase s přímými položkami). Jeho přímé položky se otevřou jako přímé barvy, pojmenované jako ve vzorníku; použitím jedné z nich se barva přidá do kresby. TraceDraw nedodává licencované vzorníky barev, ale vzorník, který vlastníte, se otevře jako jakákoli paleta. Přímé barvy v tisku a exportech V souborech PDF se každá barva stane separační barvou pojmenovanou podle ní, takže tiskárna barvu dostane. Při tisku separací dostane každá barva vlastní desku po deskách azurové, purpurové, žluté a černé. Viz Tisk. Na obrazovce a v bitmapách, souborech SVG a .cdr se přímá barva zobrazí jako svá náhrada v daném odstínu.

h: Profily kresby Výchozí nastavení nových kreseb Náhled tiskových barev
x: Správa barev Obrazovky zobrazují barvy červeným, zeleným a modrým světlem; tiskárny míchají azurovou, purpurovou, žlutou a černou barvu. Správa barev popisuje každé zařízení pomocí barevných profilů, takže barva si zachová vzhled od obrazovky až po vytištěnou stránku. Nastavení najdete v Nástroje > Správa barev, v dialogovém okně Nastavení správy barev. Nic se nezmění, dokud nekliknete na OK.  Profily kresby Karta Dokument nastavuje profily aktivní kresby. Aktuální profily ukazuje profily RGB, CMYK a stupňů šedi, které kresba právě používá. Zvolte, jak se nový profil použije: Přiřadit nový (zachovat hodnoty barev): hodnoty barev zůstanou a jejich vzhled se změní podle nového profilu; Převést (zachovat vzhled barev): barvy CMYK se převedou tak, aby v novém profilu vypadaly stejně. Zvolte profily Profil RGB, Profil CMYK a Stupně šedi. Každý seznam obsahuje výchozí profily a za nimi všechny profily nalezené v počítači. Načíst barevné profily přidá soubory profilů (.icc, .icm). Hlavní barevný režim: CMYK nebo RGB. Způsob vykreslení: jak se převedou barvy, které nelze zobrazit: Relativní kolorimetrický (výchozí), Perceptuální, Sytost nebo Absolutní kolorimetrický. Profil CMYK se ukládá s kresbou, také do souborů .cdr od verze 16. Výchozí nastavení nových kreseb Karta Výchozí nastavuje, co používají nové kresby a jak se převádějí barvy. Předvolba: hotová nastavení pro Severní Ameriku, Evropu, Japonsko nebo práci pro web a obrazovku. Uložit předvolbu uloží vaše vlastní nastavení pod zadaným Název předvolby; Odstranit předvolbu předvolbu odebere. Výchozí Profil RGB, Profil CMYK a Profil stupňů šedi, Hlavní barevný režim a Způsob vykreslení. Převod barev: Barevný modul: Modul ICC TraceDraw, který používá profily, nebo Vestavěné vzorce; Zachovat čistou černou: barvy tvořené jen černou barvou zůstanou po převodu jen černou; Převádět šedou na černou CMYK (výchozí zapnuto): šedé převedené do CMYK používají jen černou barvu; Kompenzace černého bodu (výchozí zapnuto): udrží nejtmavší odstíny od sebe odlišené. Zásady otevírání: co se stane s profilem otevíraného souboru, pro RGB, CMYK a stupně šedi: Použít vložený barevný profil, Přiřadit výchozí barevný profil nebo Převést na výchozí barevný profil. Upozornit na odlišný barevný profil a Upozornit na chybějící barevný profil zobrazí zprávu ve stavovém řádku, když má soubor jiný profil nebo žádný. Zásady importu a vkládání: Převést na barevný profil dokumentu nebo Přiřadit barevný profil dokumentu pro to, co importujete nebo vkládáte. Definice přímých barev: zda jsou přímé barvy definovány pomocí Hodnoty Lab, Hodnoty CMYK nebo Hodnoty RGB. Náhled tiskových barev Zobrazení > Nátisk barev nebo tlačítko nátisku na pravém konci stavového řádku zobrazí kresbu tak, jak by se vytiskla: barvy, které tiskové barvy CMYK nedokážou vytisknout, vypadají matněji. Na takové barvy upozorňuje také panel Barva. Bez načtených profilů převádí TraceDraw barvy vlastním modelem procesních barev na křídovém papíře.

t: Converting colors to CMYK or RGB
h: Converting the colors What is converted How the colors are worked out
x: Converting colors to CMYK or RGB A drawing often mixes colors defined in RGB (for screens) with colors defined in CMYK (for printing inks). Before you send a drawing to print, or reuse a print job on the web, Tools > Convert Colors turns every color of the selected objects, or of the whole drawing, into one model in a single step. Converting the colors To convert only some objects, select them first. Choose Tools > Convert Colors. Under Convert to, choose CMYK (the default) or RGB. Under Colors of, choose The selected objects (the default when something is selected) or The whole drawing, which also takes in the pages' backgrounds and the symbols. Tick Convert spot colors too to turn spot colors into their CMYK or RGB mix as well (off at first). Click OK. The status bar says how many colors changed. All the changes undo in one step. When every color is already in the model you chose, or nothing is selected, nothing changes. What is converted Solid fills, the stops of gradients, the colors of mesh fills, patterns and textures. Outlines, text and table cells. The colors of effects (contours, blends, extrusions, bevels, block shadows and the others) and of drop shadows. Objects inside groups and clip frames, at any depth. Bitmaps take the color mode: converted to CMYK, a picture's pixels change to show the colors the inks can print; converted to RGB, only the mode changes and the pixels stay. See Bitmap color modes. The registration color never changes, so marks still print on every plate. Spot colors stay spot colors unless you tick Convert spot colors too. A color that is already in the model stays as it is. How the colors are worked out The conversion goes through the color management profiles: the drawing's own CMYK profile when it carries one, else the RGB and CMYK profiles, the rendering intent and the black point setting of Tools > Color Management. See Color management. Tip: A color converted to CMYK and back to RGB is not the color you started with when it was too bright for the inks. Keep a copy of the drawing before converting a whole drawing.

Speciální efekty Efekty mění vzhled objektu, aniž by měnily objekt samotný: prolnutí vyplní prostor mezi dvěma objekty, kontura nakreslí kolem objektu prstence, obálka ho ohne, vysunutí mu dá objem, stín ho oddělí od stránky. Většina efektů je živá: objekt si ponechá svůj tvar a efekt se z něj kreslí, takže efekt můžete kdykoli změnit nebo odstranit. Efekty najdete v nabídce Efekty, v rozbalovací nabídce Efekty panelu nástrojů a ve vlastních panelech. Bitmapové efekty mění pixely obrázků nebo objektů kreslených jako obrázky.

h: Managing effects Other effect commands
x: The Effects panel An object can carry several live effects at once, applied one after the other. The Effects panel lists the effects of the selected object in the order they apply, from the top down. Open it with Window > Panels > Effects.  Managing effects Each row of the list has: a check box that turns the effect on or off. An effect turned off keeps its place and settings, but is not drawn, exported or printed; the effect's name, dimmed while it is off; up and down arrows that move the effect earlier or later, which changes the result (for example a contour of an envelope, or an envelope of a contour); a cross that removes the effect. Every change is one undo step. Each effect is still edited with its own tool or panel. Other effect commands Effects > Flatten Effects turns the effects of the selected objects into plain objects. Effect Picker shows a list of effects to apply to the selection. Object > Clear Effect removes the effect of the selection. Object > Copy Effect copies an effect from another object, and Clone Effect makes a clone that follows it; see Copying and cloning effects.

h: To blend two objects Blend settings Controls on the canvas Blending along a path Removing or splitting a blend Saving as .cdr
x: Blends A blend draws a series of intermediate steps between two objects, changing shape, size and color from one to the other. Use it for smooth shading, repeated patterns or a shape that turns into another. To blend two objects With the tool: Choose the Blend tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from the start object to the end object. With the panel: Select two objects. Open the Blend panel with Effects > Blend (Ctrl+F8). Set the options and click Apply.  Both objects stay objects of the drawing: move, resize or recolor either one and the steps follow. Deleting the end object removes the blend. Blend settings With a blend selected, every change on the property bar or in the panel applies at once. Blend steps: the number of steps (5 at first, up to 999). Spacing, for a blend on a path: the distance between steps; the number of steps follows from the length of the path. Rotation: turns the steps progressively; Loop turns them about the middle between the two objects instead. Acceleration: the object slider makes the steps crowd towards one end; the color slider does the same for the colors. Apply to sizing makes the object acceleration change the sizes too, and Link acceleration keeps the two sliders together. Reset puts both back to even. Color Blend: Direct (straight from one color to the other), Clockwise or Counterclockwise (around the color wheel). The tool's property bar has the steps, rotation and the two accelerations. Controls on the canvas Pick a blend with the Blend tool (click its start or end object, or a step) to show its controls: a square on the start object, a crossed square on the end object, the line between them and two sliders on it, the object acceleration above and the color acceleration below. Drag a slider toward the start or the end to crowd the steps or the colors there. The blend follows live, each drag is one undo step, and the property bar follows. A slider goes as far one way as the other: at 100 % the middle step sits right by the start object, at -100 % right by the end object. Drag an end square to move its object, so the blend changes direction. Drop it on another object to make that object the new start or end, with the blend's settings. The object acceleration moves the steps toward one end also when the blend follows no path. A bitmap effect on the start object keeps the blend drawn. Blending along a path Select the blend. Click New path in the Blend panel and click a curve. The steps follow the curve. Rotate all objects turns each step along the curve, and Blend along full path places the first and last steps at the ends of the curve. Removing or splitting a blend Clear blend removes the steps and leaves both objects. Break apart turns the steps into objects of their own, grouped. Object > Break Blend Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same. Saving as .cdr A blend saved as .cdr (version 9 or later) stays a blend: the file holds the two objects and the blend record between them, so the program that opens the file shows the steps and lets you change the blend. The steps, spacing and the two objects go into the file; acceleration, rotation, a path and the colour direction come back in TraceDraw (version 14 or later), other programs start from their defaults.

h: To add a contour Contour settings
x: Contours A contour draws evenly spaced copies of an object's outline inside it, outside it, or to its center, like the lines of a map. It is a live effect: change the object and the contour follows. To add a contour With the tool: Choose the Contour tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object: away from its middle for an outside contour, towards it for an inside one. The further you drag, the larger the spacing. With the panel: Select an object. Open the Contour panel with Effects > Contour (Ctrl+F9). Set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot take a contour. Contour settings The property bar and the panel show the settings of the selected contour and change it at once. To center, Inside or Outside (at first). Steps: 3 at first, up to 999. To center makes as many as fit. Offset: the distance between steps (2 mm at first). Corners: mitered (sharp, at first), round or beveled. Color direction: direct, clockwise or counterclockwise around the color wheel, from the object's colors to the last step's. The fill and outline colors of the last step (white and black at first). An object without a fill gives unfilled steps. Object acceleration and color acceleration (-100 to 100%) crowd the steps or the colors towards the object or towards the last step. Outside steps are drawn behind the object, inside steps in front of it. Clear contour removes the contour; Break apart turns the steps into objects, grouped beside the object. Object > Break Contour Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same.

h: To distort an object Distortion settings
x: Distortion The Distort tool bends an object's outline in three ways: push and pull (spikes or petals), zipper (zigzag teeth) and twister (a swirl). It is a live effect: you can change, move or remove the distortion at any time, and the object keeps its own outline. To distort an object Choose the Distort tool from the Effects flyout. Choose the kind on the property bar. Drag on the object. The distortion is centered where you start. Push and pull: drag right to push the nodes out (spiky shapes with hollow sides), left to pull them in (rounded petals). Zipper: the further you drag, the taller the teeth. Twister: drag around the starting point; full turns count. The center of a selected distortion shows as a diamond: drag it to move the center. Dragging again replaces the distortion; an object has at most one. Groups and bitmaps are not distorted.
